Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Global Assurance Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Assurance Holdings' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; and David Kim, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Global Assurance Holdings' performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust net written premiums growth across our lines of business, improving loss ratio trends through disciplined pricing and frequency mitigation, prudent asset allocation supporting steady investment returns, favorable realized and unrealized gains on our portfolio, and strategic capital deployment plans that balance shareholder returns with growth opportunities. Our focus on underwriting excellence and technological innovation continues to yield positive outcomes as we navigate a dynamic market environment.

Michael Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.25 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included double-digit net written premiums growth, controlled loss ratios despite catastrophe activity, and resilient investment income. Our combined ratio was 98.2%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. Investment income for the quarter was $212 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with an RBC ratio of 520%.

Let me start with our top-line performance, which continues to demonstrate the strength of our underwriting discipline and market positioning. Net written premiums—or NWP—grew 13.2% year-over-year to $4.8 billion in the quarter, marking our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. This outpaced the industry average of around 9% as reported by AM Best for the broader P&C sector, driven by a combination of rate increases averaging 8.5% across the book, new business wins up 22% from last year, and industry-leading retention rates of 93.8%—up 110 basis points sequentially.

Breaking this down by line of business, personal lines, which represent 44% of our total NWP, delivered solid 10.4% growth to $2.1 billion, slightly ahead of the 9% industry benchmark from Verisk Analytics data. This was split between auto at +9.2% and homeowners/dwellings at +12.1%. Personal auto growth was fueled by a 7.8% rate increase—the third consecutive quarter of mid-single-digit hikes—amid escalating claims severity from inflation in OEM parts and labor, now running 15% above pre-pandemic levels per CCC Intelligent Solutions indices. Volume was up 4.5% on the back of our Telematics Advantage program, now penetrating 28% of our policies, similar to Progressive's Snapshot model but enhanced with AI-driven risk scoring from our partnership with LexisNexis. Retention held steady at 92.5%, with new business submissions up 18% in telematics-optimized states like Florida and Texas. Regionally, U.S. growth was 10.8%, while our UK book grew 6% despite softer market conditions there. Homeowners accelerated to 12.1% growth, benefiting from 10.2% average rate action after secondary perils like hail and wildfires drove a 5-point loss ratio deterioration YTD. Bookings expanded 7% via bundled offerings with our smart home IoT integrations, akin to Allstate's Drivewise but focused on mitigation credits—reducing modeled cat losses by 12%. U.S. exposure grew robustly in catastrophe-prone Southeast markets, up 14%, offset by disciplined non-renewals in high-risk California zones amid the FAIR Plan spillover. Internationally, our Australian homeowners book added 8% on reinsurance treaty renewals at favorable terms. We're leaning into embedded insurance via API partnerships with platforms like Hippo and Lemonade's tech stack, targeting millennials with parametric triggers for micro-disruptions, which should add 2-3 points to personal lines growth in FY24.

Commercial lines, our highest-margin segment at 40% of NWP, surged 16.7% to $1.9 billion, well above the 12% market growth tracked by Carrier Management. This reflects our leadership in middle-market renewals and excess & surplus capacity. Standard commercial P&C was up 15.2% to $1.4 billion, driven by 11% rate gains—the highest since 2007 hardening cycles—against a backdrop of social inflation in liability claims, with jury awards up 22% per Jury Verdict Research. Policy count grew 6.8% through our small business accelerator platform, which uses machine learning for instant quoting, mirroring Travelers' commercial appetite. Retention hit 95.2%, bolstered by multi-year deals now at 22% of the book. U.S. regions shone: Northeast industrial up 18% on supply chain hardening, Midwest agribusiness +14% despite drought normalization. Workers' comp was a standout at +20.1% growth, with rates up 9.5% and payroll exposure expanding 8% via payroll API integrations with ADP and Paychex. Our Experience Modification Rating focus kept loss ratios at 78%, below peers, in a market where NCCI data shows comp severity rising 12% YoY. Regionally, Europe contributed 11% growth on Brexit-related supply chain policies, while Asia-Pacific—led by Singapore and Japan—added 22% via our new joint venture with MSIG, targeting construction risks. Our Quantum Pricing Engine, deployed across 85% of commercial submissions, dynamically adjusts for inflation proxies like PPI and regional wage indices, delivering 3 points of organic growth uplift.

Rounding out the portfolio, specialty & reinsurance grew 22.3% to $800 million, capitalizing on capacity-constrained markets and our quota-share placements. This segment, 17% of NWP, benefits from our A+ AM Best rating and diversified retrocession. Directors & officers (D&O) rose +28% on 14% rate increases amid SEC scrutiny and cyber-adjacent liabilities—similar to dynamics boosting AIG's specialty book. New business was up 35%, with $150 million in attachments from Fortune 1000 clients. Cyber NWP jumped 32%, riding the ransomware wave (up 40% per Chainalysis), with our parametric cyber product—launched Q1—now covering 15% of writings. Property cat grew 19%, post-1/1 reinsurance renewals at 5% lower cession rates, freeing $200 million in capital. Reinsurance assumed was +18%, selectively from programs like our 40% quota-share on PartnerRe's U.S. casualty tower. Regionally, this was global: U.S. +24%, EMEA +20% on marine hull amid Red Sea disruptions, and LatAm +15% via Brazil facultative placements. We've allocated $500 million to opportunistic cat bonds via our Bermuda SPV, akin to RenaissanceRe's model, targeting ILS returns of 8-10%. This de-risks our balance sheet while funding specialty expansion, with ROE targets of 25%+.

Across LOBs, our NWP growth reflects a hardening market—global P&C rates up 7.9% per McKinsey—juxtaposed with our 4.2% earned premium growth lag due to 12-month collection lags. Ceded premiums rose modestly 2% as % of gross, thanks to efficient tower structures post-1/1 renewals. Inflation remains headwind number one, with auto physical damage costs +16% and property rebuilds +11% per Xactimate. Looking forward, we guide FY24 NWP growth to 12-14%, with Q4 acceleration from holiday-season personal lines and mid-year commercial renewals. Our ATLAS analytics platform—now processing 10 petabytes of telematics and claims data—positions us for sustained 10%+ organic growth through 2025, outpacing peers like The Hartford or W.R. Berkley.

As we dive deeper into our core P&C segment results, I'd like to unpack our loss ratio trends and the key drivers behind them. The loss ratio stood at 92.3% on a calendar year basis—up 380 basis points year-over-year from 88.5%, and 210 basis points above our long-term target of 90%. To provide full context, this compares to accident year loss ratio of 91.8%, which benefited from about 50 basis points of favorable prior year development, primarily in our commercial auto book where we saw better-than-expected BI settlements. For perspective, this is in line with peers like Progressive and Travelers, who've reported similar pressures, but our underlying ex-cat loss ratio improved to 87.6%, a 140 basis point enhancement from Q3 2023, driven by disciplined pricing and frequency mitigation.

Claims frequency remained stable to slightly improving across most books, but we saw pockets of upside pressure. Overall personal lines frequency was flat quarter-over-quarter at 5.8 claims per 100 exposure units, but up 1.2% year-over-year. In personal auto—our largest line at 42% of earned premiums—frequency ticked up 2.1% YoY to 7.2 claims/100 cars, largely due to a post-pandemic rebound in vehicle miles traveled, now running about 12% above 2019 levels per DOT data. This mirrors industry trends, with ISO estimating a 1.5-2.5% uptick across the US private passenger auto market. On the positive side, our homeowners frequency improved 3% YoY to 4.1 claims/100 policies, thanks to proactive mitigation. We've rolled out enhanced weather alert integrations via our app, partnering with The Weather Company, which reduced wind/hail claims by 8% in high-risk hail alley states like Texas and Nebraska. Commercial lines frequency was a bright spot, down 4% YoY to 3.9 claims/100 units, aided by stricter underwriting in workers' comp, where we've layered in occupational health data from partners like Verisk.

Severity remains the bigger headwind, up 6.8% YoY across the portfolio to an average of $18,400 per claim. This is driven by persistent inflation across repair costs, medical expenses, and litigation trends. In auto physical damage, severity surged 9.2% YoY to $12,500 per claim, fueled by a 15% rise in OEM parts prices—think semiconductor shortages lingering into EV transitions—and labor rates hitting $55/hour in key markets, per CCC Intelligent Solutions data. Bodily injury severity was up 7.5% to $42,000, with social inflation adding fuel: we've seen a 12% increase in jury awards in nuclear verdict states like Florida and California, consistent with Wyser-Pratte reports. Homeowners severity climbed 5.4% YoY to $22,800 per claim, pressured by rising replacement costs—now 25% above 2020 levels per CoreLogic—and water damage payouts amid aging infrastructure. Commercial multi-peril severity rose 8% to $65,000, with large losses over $1M comprising 15% of total paid claims, up from 12% last year.

Catastrophes amplified these dynamics: Q3 NAT cats added 450 basis points to the loss ratio, totaling $450 million pre-tax, dominated by California wildfires ($220M, impacting 15,000 policies) and Hurricane Helene remnants in the Southeast ($150M). This compares to $280M in Q3 2023, but our ex-cat underlying trend shows resilience. Regionally, US (85% of premiums): Northeast and Midwest saw milder weather, keeping ex-cat loss ratios at 86%, but Southeast wildfire and storm activity pushed it to 94%. California remains challenged at 96%, prompting a 12% rate increase filing with the DOI. Europe (10%): UK motor severity up 7% due to parts inflation post-Brexit, but frequency down 2% from our telematics program. Floods in Germany added €45M, or 200 bps. Other International (5%): Australia bushfires were contained, limiting impact to 3% of regional premiums.

We're not standing still. Pricing actions have captured $1.2B in annualized premium growth, with indicated rate needs now at 8.5% for personal auto renewals—on top of the 9.2% we took in Q2. Our usage-based insurance (UBI) penetration hit 28% in personal auto, akin to Progressive's Snapshot, reducing frequency 5-7% for safe drivers via our GA Drive telematics, which now uses ML algorithms to score behaviors in real-time. On claims handling, we've invested $50M in GenAI-powered adjudication, cutting cycle times 25% and large loss identification accuracy to 92% via partnerships with Cytora. This shaved 80 bps off loss adjustment expenses. Reinsurance renewal was favorable: our $500M XS tower at 2.5% attachment with 20% ceding commission, providing $2B in NAT cat protection. Looking forward, we expect Q4 loss ratio of 90-92%, with ex-cat at 88%, assuming normalized weather. Our 2025 plan targets 89% through 10% pricing, 3% frequency reduction via expanded UBI to 40% penetration, and severity caps via preferred repair networks negotiating 10% off labor rates. We're also de-risking high-litigation exposures, non-renewing 5% of our California HO book. While near-term pressures from severity and cats are real, our underlying trajectory is improving, positioning us for mid-teens ROEs.

Before moving on, let me provide an update on our investment portfolio performance, starting with our asset allocation strategy, which remains the cornerstone of our asset-liability management—or ALM—framework. With $258 billion in general account invested assets as of quarter-end, our portfolio is designed to deliver stable, risk-adjusted returns while ensuring robust liability matching for our $210 billion in insurance reserves. This quarter, we generated $2.8 billion in net investment income annualized, up 4% year-over-year, driven by higher reinvestment yields amid the Fed's steady 5.25-5.50% policy rate and modestly widening credit spreads.

Fixed income continues to dominate our allocation at 72%, or $186 billion, down slightly from 75% a year ago as we tactically rotated into higher-yielding alternatives. This segment yielded 4.2% in Q3, with a book yield of 4.8% and an effective duration of 6.2 years—precisely matched to our intermediate-duration liabilities, minimizing interest rate risk under our dynamic ALM model. U.S. Treasuries and agencies comprise 22% of fixed income at $41 billion: we hold 18% in 10-year Treasuries yielding 4.3% and 4% in agency MBS, benefiting from the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate Index's 2.1% total return this quarter. Amid persistent inflation at 3.2% CPI, we've extended modestly in the 7-10 year bucket to lock in rates before any potential Fed pivot. Investment-grade corporates are 38% at $71 billion, with 85% rated A or better per SVO NAIC designations. Spreads widened 15 bps to 125 bps over Treasuries, boosting new money yields to 5.6%. We've overweighted financials like JPMorgan and Berkshire Hathaway paper, given their resilient balance sheets, while underweighting cyclical industrials. High-yield and structured credit at 15% or $28 billion yield 6.8%, including BBB-rated CLOs and RMBS, where we've seen attractive risk-adjusted spreads of 350 bps. Delinquency rates remain low at 1.2% per Moody's data, supporting our 2% allocation to private credit via funds like Ares and Owl Rock. Municipals and other at 25% or $46 billion, tax-exempt munis at 4.1% yield provide state tax efficiency for our U.S. annuity block, with a focus on essential services issuers. Regionally, 65% is U.S.-centric for P&C matching, 20% Eurozone sovereigns and Pfandbriefe yielding 3.2% for our European life ops, and 15% in Asia ex-Japan IG credits like Samsung bonds, hedging yen exposure via FX forwards.

Equities represent 13% at $33.5 billion, up from 11% last year, targeting long-term growth for our variable annuity separate accounts and surplus capital. Q3 total return was 5.7%, outpacing the S&P 500's 4.9% amid tech rotation. Our Sharpe ratio here stands at 0.85, reflecting disciplined active management. Public equities are 85% of the class at $28.5 billion: 40% U.S. large-cap like dividend aristocrats Procter & Gamble, 30% global developed MSCI EAFE, and 30% emerging markets with a China overweight via MSCI China ETFs, navigating regulatory headwinds. Preferreds and convertibles at 15% or $5 billion yield 5.9%, enhancing income with equity upside. We've capped equities at 15% per our RBC optimization model to maintain a 450% risk-based capital ratio, well above regulatory thresholds. In Europe, Solvency II constraints limit us to 10% there, favoring UCITS-compliant ETFs.

Alternatives have grown to 15% or $38.5 billion—our fastest-expanding sleeve—delivering an 8.2% annualized return since inception, with low correlation (0.25) to fixed income. This shift addresses the hunt for yield in a post-ZIRP world, where 10-year swap rates hover at 4.1%. Real assets are 40% of alts at $15.4 billion: core real estate like multifamily via Blackstone REITs at 6.5% cap rates, and infrastructure with a 40% stake in Brookfield renewables yielding 7.2%, inflation-linked for longevity risk hedging. Private equity and credit at 35% or $13.5 billion include commitments to KKR direct lending and Apollo private equity vintage 2022-2024 funds, with DPI of 1.2x and NAV growth accelerated 12% QoQ on realizations. Hedge funds and other at 25% or $9.6 billion feature multi-strat funds like Citadel Wellington (market-neutral) and reinsurance sidecars, providing cat bond exposure with a low 0.5% loss ratio YTD. Regionally, Asia alternatives (20%) focus on Indian infrastructure via GIC partnerships, while our U.S. P&C book leans into Florida hurricane-linked ILS for yield pickup.

Portfolio-wide, we're navigating a higher-for-longer rate environment with 85% liquidity in cash equivalents and T-bills, positioning for opportunistic buys if spreads widen further (ICE BofA HY index at 380 bps). Yields have risen 50 bps YoY, but volatility—VIX averaging 16—prompts our use of interest rate swaps ($10 billion notional) and equity total return swaps to hedge tail risks. Technically, we've rolled out an AI-driven portfolio optimizer using BlackRock's Aladdin platform, integrated with our proprietary ALM engine, improving attribution analysis and shaving 5 bps off tracking error vs. our custom liability benchmark. Strategically, de-risking life reserves with LDI overlays match our $120 billion deferred annuities, reducing PV01 to under $2 million per 100 bps shift. ESG integration sees 25% of new commitments SFDR Article 8/9 compliant, targeting green bonds and sustainable PE without yield sacrifice. Alternatives boost ROE by 150 bps, supporting our 12-14% target while maintaining AA- ratings from S&P and AM Best. Regional tailwinds include U.S. growth from FIA sales; Europe Solvency II matching adjustments at 2.5%; Asia expansion via joint ventures with Ping An. Our allocation balances yield, liquidity, and resilience, positioning us for sustained 4.5-5% portfolio returns and 10% EPS growth guidance.

Diving deeper into our investment results, specifically realized and unrealized gains and losses, which contributed a net positive $85 million to our bottom line this quarter. Our $52.4 billion general account investment portfolio remains the engine of our spread business. With new money rates holding steady around 4.8%—thanks to our disciplined ALM framework—we're navigating a higher-for-longer rate environment effectively. At quarter-end, fixed income remains our core at 72% or $37.7 billion, predominantly investment-grade corporates (45%), U.S. Treasuries and agencies (18%), and RMBS at 9%. Equities make up 14% or $7.3 billion, tilted toward high-quality dividend payers in financials and consumer staples. Alternatives, including direct lending and core-plus real estate, comprise 10% or $5.2 billion, while short-duration cash equivalents round out the rest at 4%. Our book yield expanded 15 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 4.65%, reflecting the successful deployment of $2.1 billion in portfolio maturities into higher-yielding assets amid spread compression in the IG corporate market.

In Q3, we booked $142 million in net realized gains, a 24% increase from $115 million in Q3 2023 and up sequentially from $98 million in Q2. This was driven by tactical sales across three key areas. First, we realized $65 million in gains from trimming our equity position in S&P 500-tracking names, capitalizing on the 5.2% rally in the index—sectors like technology and industrials, where we rotated out of overweights in semis like NVIDIA and into more defensive healthcare exposures. This enhanced our dividend yield from 2.8% to 3.1% while de-risking ahead of potential Fed pauses. Second, in fixed income, we harvested $52 million from selective sales in the long-duration end of our agency MBS bucket. With convexity working in our favor as rates stabilized post the April payroll surprise, we locked in gains on securities purchased at a discount during the 2022 bear market. Average realized gain per trade was 3.2%, well above our 2% hurdle rate, including $18 million from Fannie Mae 30-year UMBS where prepayment speeds slowed to 12 CPR amid elevated mortgage rates at 6.9%. Third, our alternatives sleeve delivered $25 million in realizations, primarily from two direct lending deals in the Midwest healthcare sector—exits yielding IRR north of 12%, beating our 9-11% target. Year-to-date, realized gains total $365 million, positioning us favorably against peers like MetLife, who reported only $210 million YTD amid their heavier legacy bond holdings.

These realizations are part of our Quarterly Portfolio Optimization Initiative (QPOI), leveraging our proprietary ALMIS system—enhanced last year with AI-driven scenario modeling from BlackRock's Aladdin platform. This allowed us to stress-test 10,000 rate paths, identifying $300 million in high-conviction trades pre-execution. Regionally, U.S.-centric realizations dominated at 82%, but we saw $15 million from European HY credits, where ECB tightening compressed spreads by 45 bps to 350 bps.

For unrealized gains and losses, we recorded a $57 million net unrealized loss this quarter, narrowing dramatically from the $312 million loss in Q3 2023 when the 10-year Treasury surged 75 bps. Our portfolio's mark-to-market declined 0.11% quarter-over-quarter, but remains up 2.4% YTD on a total return basis. The drag came primarily from duration extension in fixed income: our effective duration ticked up to 5.8 years from 5.4, exposing us to the 22 bps rise in the 10-year yield to 4.35%. Investment-grade corporates saw a $110 million unrealized loss, as credit spreads widened 8 bps to 112 bps on the Bloomberg U.S. Corporate Index, hit by sector rotation out of autos and energy. Equities contributed a $45 million gain, buoyed by resilient earnings from dividend aristocrats like Procter & Gamble and JPMorgan, offsetting volatility in the Nasdaq. RMBS unrealizeds were flat at -$12 million, benefiting from technical support as supply dried up with originations down 18% YoY. On a statutory basis, our unrealized loss position improved to -$420 million, or just 0.8% of portfolio NAV, versus peers like Prudential's 1.4%. This reflects our proactive hedging: we layered in $1.2 billion in Treasury futures and payer swaptions during Q2, capping duration at 6.2 years in a 5% rate shock scenario. In alternatives, unrealized gains swelled to +$180 million, driven by real estate appreciation in Sun Belt logistics assets amid e-commerce tailwinds.

Strategically, these dynamics underscore our Enhanced Yield Resilience Program (EYRP), launched in 2023, which targets a 50/30/20 split across IG, HY/EM debt, and alternatives by year-end. We've increased EM exposure to 7% ($3.7 billion), harvesting 120 bps of pickup over U.S. IG, with strong performance in LatAm sovereigns like Brazil's 10-year at 11.2% yield. Regionally, North America drove 65% of gains, Europe 20% bolstered by UK gilts post-BOE cuts, and Asia-Pacific 10%, where JGB duration trades added alpha amid yen weakness. Looking ahead, we expect realized gains to moderate to $110-130 million in Q4 as we hold core positions through earnings season, but unrealizeds could swing with Fed dots—our base case assumes two 25 bps cuts by December, lifting equities 4-6% and narrowing our unrealized deficit to under $200 million. We're well-positioned with $4.5 billion in dry powder for opportunistic buys if spreads blow out beyond 130 bps. Our investment results delivered a 4.2% total return, outpacing the Barclays U.S. Aggregate's 0.1% and our 3.9% liability yield, expanding spreads by 12 bps to 83 bps. This discipline supports our 11-13% ROE guidance and $1.2 billion share repurchase authorization.

Finally, on our forward-looking capital deployment strategy, let me recap our fortress balance sheet, which provides the foundation for these plans. We hold $4.2 billion in deployable capital, up 12% year-over-year, supported by our industry-leading RBC ratio of 520%—well above our 400% target—and a pristine Solvency II ratio of 220% in our European book. Adjusted operating ROE stands at 14.2% for the first three quarters, on track to meet our 13-15% full-year guidance, even amid persistent inflation pressures on auto and property claims.

Our capital allocation philosophy remains disciplined and shareholder-friendly: first, maintain optimal capital strength; second, return capital via dividends and buybacks; third, fuel organic growth through new products and tech investments; and fourth, pursue accretive inorganic opportunities like tuck-in acquisitions. We target a 40-50% total shareholder yield this year, blending dividends, repurchases, and growth. With interest rates stabilizing around the 4-5% range for 10-year Treasuries—benefiting our $25 billion fixed-income portfolio yielding 4.8%—we're generating $850 million in annual recurring investment income, giving us ample dry powder.

Shareholder returns: We've executed $450 million in share repurchases YTD at an average price of $48 per share, retiring 9.5 million shares or 4.2% of our float. This is opportunistic, given our 15% discount to embedded value per share of $62. Our board just authorized an additional $650 million program, bringing the full-year total to $1.1 billion—roughly 25% of our deployable capital. Concurrently, we increased our quarterly dividend by 8% to $0.35 per share, implying a 2.9% yield at current levels and a 45% payout ratio on operating earnings. This reflects confidence in our mid-teens EPS growth trajectory, driven by 3% premium growth and a 92.5% agate combined ratio.

For organic investments, we're deploying $300 million—or 7% of deployable capital—into initiatives emphasizing digital transformation and adjacency expansion to counter softening commercial lines pricing (down 2-3% in P&C per recent Carrier Management data). In Q4, we'll roll out "Global CyberShield Pro," a parametric cyber insurance product targeting mid-market enterprises with $5-50 million in revenue. Priced at a 15% premium to traditional policies, it features real-time API-triggered payouts for ransomware events, underwritten via our proprietary ML models that have reduced loss ratios by 25% in pilots. Initial targets: U.S. healthcare and manufacturing, where cyber claims surged 42% YoY per our analytics. We project $150 million in gross written premiums in Year 1, scaling to $500 million by 2026 at a 95% combined ratio. Responding to escalating NAT CAT losses—up 18% globally in the first nine months per Swiss Re sigma—we're launching "Resilience Home Plus" in the U.S. Southeast and Australia. This usage-based personal lines product integrates IoT telematics for 10-20% dynamic pricing discounts, bundled with parametric flood coverage. Backed by $100 million in reinsurance from Swiss Re and Munich Re at 45% cession rates, it addresses the 30% underinsurance gap in high-risk zones. $150 million is earmarked for cloud migration to AWS and Snowflake, plus embedding GenAI via partnerships like Guidewire's Eden AI suite. This targets a 200 bps expense ratio improvement to 28% by 2025, automating 40% of claims handling and boosting straight-through processing to 85%. Early wins: Our Insurtech accelerator with Plug and Play Ventures has surfaced three startups, including a blockchain-based parametric platform now in beta for Asia-Pacific agriculture. Regionally, U.S. P&C (65% of GWP) drives 60% of these investments amid hardening reinsurance markets; Europe (20%) focuses on Solvency II-compliant ESG products like green energy liability, capturing the EU's $1 trillion sustainable finance push; and APAC (15%), via our joint venture with Ping An, emphasizes microinsurance for India's 500 million underserved, projecting 25% CAGR.

For inorganic growth, with M&A multiples normalizing to 1.1x embedded value (down from 1.4x peaks), we're positioned for 2-3 tuck-ins totaling $500 million. These prioritize adjacencies in high-growth niches like cyber, health tech, and specialty lines, targeting 12-15% ROE accretion within 18 months. In Q3, we closed on Harbor Specialty for $250 million, a New York-based excess & surplus carrier with $180 million GWP in D&O and cyber. Synergies include $40 million in annual cost savings from platform integration and cross-selling into our 2 million commercial policyholders. Pro forma, it lifts our E&S market share to 4.5% per AM Best, with loss ratios 300 bps below peers at 58%. Pipeline highlights: We're advancing a $200 million bid for a European life reinsurer with strong embedded value in the Nordics, hedging longevity risk amid aging populations. In the U.S., eyeing a cyber insurtech akin to Corvus for $100 million, adding ML-driven underwriting to our book. APAC focus: Potential tie-up with a Southeast Asian microinsurer to tap Indonesia's 7% digital penetration growth. These deals maintain our 10% annual book value per share growth target, diversified across P&C (70%), life/annuities (20%), and group benefits (10%). We avoid mega-mergers, sticking to low-risk bolt-ons with >20% IRR hurdles.

In this environment—where inflation lingers at 3.5% driving 5-7% claim severity increases, yet rate adequacy improves combined ratios to sub-92%—our strategy balances defense with offense. We're de-risking via 55% catastrophe aggregate cover at $1.75 billion attachment points, while leaning into secular tailwinds: cyber premiums growing 25% globally per McKinsey, parametric adoption rising 40%, and insurtech ROI hitting 3x for early adopters. Looking ahead, we expect $2.5-3 billion in deployable capital by year-end, supporting 15% EPS growth to $4.20. Risks include prolonged high rates compressing annuity spreads (our VA block yields 5.2% hedged), but upsides from AI efficiencies could add 100 bps to ROE.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial lines segment. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including expanded usage-based insurance and AI-enhanced pricing models that have driven our NWP growth and kept underlying loss ratios trending favorably ex-cat.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on loss ratio trends, particularly the drivers like frequency and severity?

Michael Chen: Good morning, John. As I detailed earlier, our calendar year loss ratio was 92.3%, up 380 bps YoY due to severity pressures and cats, but our ex-cat underlying improved 140 bps to 87.6%. Frequency was stable overall, with personal auto up 2.1% on VMT rebound but homeowners down 3% from app-based mitigations. Severity rose 6.8% portfolio-wide to $18,400 per claim, driven by 9.2% auto PD inflation and social inflation in BI. Cats added 450 bps, but our initiatives like GenAI claims and UBI are positioning us for 88-90% ex-cat in Q4.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of higher interest rates on your investment portfolio and business?

David Kim: Good morning, Emily. Higher rates have been a tailwind, pushing our book yield to 4.8% and enabling $142 million in Q3 realized gains from tactical sales in equities and MBS. Our 72% fixed income allocation matches liabilities with 6.2-year duration, and alternatives at 15% deliver 8.2% returns. Unrealized losses narrowed to $57 million net, hedged effectively. This supports stable spreads and our 4.5-5% return target.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes around cyber risk on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Robert. Regulatory scrutiny like SEC rules on disclosures is driving D&O and cyber demand, where we grew 32% in NWP. We're enhancing our parametric cyber product with ML underwriting, targeting 95% combined ratios.
